standard.title: Technology Enabling Science and Vice Versa
standard.description: investigate how advances in technologies enable advances in science, and how science has contributed to developments in technologies and engineering
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have examined how science knowledge is applied to meet needs and solve problems (earlier H-strand bands). They now examine the bidirectional relationship — technology enabling science and science enabling technology.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate examples of the bidirectional science-technology relationship — identifying both cases where technology enabled new scientific discovery and cases where scientific understanding enabled new technology.

nodes.label: Technology advances enable scientific advances
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how specific technology advances made previously impossible scientific observations or experiments possible, and identify what knowledge was unlocked by each technology.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe at least two cases where a technology advance enabled a scientific advance, explaining the connection between the technology capability and the knowledge it made possible.
nodes.typical_width: Students examine how imaging technologies (MRI, CT, PET) improved understanding of body system interactions; how monitoring technologies enabled tracking of greenhouse gas emissions; how particle accelerators and electron microscopes enabled exploration at atomic and sub-atomic scales; and trace the technology-to-knowledge pathway in each case.
wider: Examine how developments in imaging technologies have improved understanding of body system functions and interactions — tracing specific technology improvements to specific knowledge gains
Research how technological advances in monitoring greenhouse gas emissions contributed to the reinstatement of traditional fire management practices as an emissions reduction strategy
Explore how understanding of the nature of matter and energy has changed as modern technology has enabled exploration from black holes to sub-atomic particles
success_criteria: Describes at least two cases where a technology advance enabled a scientific discovery
Explains what specific capability the technology provided and what knowledge it unlocked

nodes.label: Scientific knowledge enables technology development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how specific scientific knowledge enabled the development of technologies — tracing the science-to-engineering pathway in real examples.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe at least two technologies that were developed based on specific scientific understanding, explaining the science that enabled each.
nodes.typical_width: Students examine Australian technological contributions (cochlear implant, bionic eye, spray-on skin, wi-fi); explain how properties of electromagnetic radiation underlie technologies including radar, mobile phones and medical imaging; and describe how understanding of radioactivity led to medical and industrial applications.
wider: Consider the impact of Australian technological developments — cochlear implant, bionic eye, spray-on skin, wi-fi — and examine the scientific knowledge that made each possible
Examine how properties of electromagnetic radiation relate to specific uses: radar, medicine, mobile communications, remote sensing and microwave cooking
Explore how advances in understanding radioactivity and radioisotopes led to new medical and industrial applications

response_modes.reason: Students readily identify one science-to-technology example without seeing the variety of pathways — from physics to medical device, from radioactivity to nuclear medicine, from wave theory to communications technology. The Australian contributions direction provides a nationally grounded set of cases that span multiple science disciplines and reveal the breadth of science-to-application pathways.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Australian technology contributions provide a nationally relevant direction with strong elaboration grounding. The EM radiation applications direction connects wave model knowledge from AC9S9U04 to real technology in a cross-strand way.
success_criteria: Describes at least two technologies enabled by specific scientific knowledge
Explains the science-to-application pathway for each — what knowledge was applied and how
